legend: This unique clinical subtype affects the bone and soft tissues of the orbital region and may result in profound asymmetry. Café-au-lait spots and conventional cutaneous neurofibromas are also present in this patient.

legend: This axial CT using bone windows highlights prominent bone remodelling, facial neurofibromatosis, and proptosis associated with a large orbital neurofibroma in a patient with neurofibromatosis type 1.
Orbital neurofibromas frequently have plexiform components and may intimately involve ocular adnexa such as the lacrimal gland as in this example.

diagnosis: Pilocytic astrocytoma of the optic nerve
legend: Coronal T1-weighted MRI demonstrates an enhancing mass expanding the right optic nerve. The optic nerve is a favoured site for glioma development in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1.

A A near-infrared image of the posterior pole of a patient affected by neurofibromatosis type 1, showing multiple choroidal abnormalities (red chevrons). B The choroidal abnormalities, histologically consisting of variable mixtures of hyperplastic Schwann cells, melanocytes, and ganglion cells localized to the choroid, are completely asymptomatic and undetectable by conventional ophthalmoscopy, as shown in this colour fundus image of the same eye. Note that several retinal vascular abnormalities are also present.
Lisch nodules are small hamartomas that involve the anterior surface of the iris and are present in the majority of patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 at some point.
